checks.name: A backend evaluation produces an immutable receipt from actual returned evidence
Live evaluation refuses stale worker references before using the backend
Async backend work cannot rewrite the evaluation intent through shared mutable input
An evaluation for another runtime model or dataset cannot masquerade as the requested work
The adapter compares actual preprocessing, method and configuration rather than echoing intent
Training output must identify its real session and the checkpoint it reports
Checkpoint loading admits a new runtime identity for matching bytes and rejects observed mismatches
A rejected newly loaded handle receives explicit compensating cleanup, without successful load evidence
Cleanup failure cannot replace a rejected-load error or assert successful disposal
Reusing a published runtime handle for different checkpoint bytes is refused without deleting its owner
An observer failure cannot prevent cleanup of an unpublished loaded handle
Malformed accessor-backed output is rejected without executing the getter
Failed evaluation does not pretend to roll back backend lifetime; explicit disposal owns cleanup
Disposal cannot report successful cleanup for another handle or a failed release
A confirmed disposed reference cannot be evaluated or disposed twice through the adapter
Conformance and CLI imports create no process even when spawning is blocked
A valid report is detached and frozen; arguments are literal and snapshotted before awaiting
Exit one preserves a valid failed conformance report
Explicit skipped coverage remains partial instead of becoming a passing report
Malformed JSON, contradictory counts and contradictory status are protocol failures
Unexpected exits cannot turn an earlier passing report into successful conformance
Deadline and stdout bounds terminate the owned child rather than wait for it
Error diagnostics retain a bounded stderr tail
Invalid JSON options and an unavailable interpreter fail explicitly
CLI reads JSON files and exits distinctly for success, conformance failure and input failure
Root import never loads optional entry points; a deferred adapter import loads only when reached
Importing every public entry point starts no worker; explicit trainer construction is the first spawn
New identity-aware evaluations produce an explicit v2 inference receipt with separate checkpoint audit data
V2 coverage permits optimizer-only and container changes while retaining the original checkpoint for audit
Changed weights, fitted preprocessing, architecture or inference code cannot borrow prior v2 coverage
V1 receipts are preserved rather than silently upgraded, and retain exact-checkpoint coverage
Missing, mixed and contradictory identity evidence fails closed without dropping back to checkpoint matching
Malformed identity claims are rejected when recording or reopening evidence
Identity-aware new handles require inspection before train/load publication or evaluation
Explicit verifyModel always asks an inspector, including for legacy refs
Live mutation hidden behind stale metadata is caught before evaluation or explicit verification
An evaluator cannot mutate the inspected model during work and still publish an old receipt
A newly returned model is inspected before publication, and its original fingerprint cannot be rewritten
Successful identity-aware evaluation is inspected before and after work, and disposal is inspected first
Training continuation receives an immutable copy of the verified source and configuration
Inference equivalence never permits a published live handle to change its full checkpoint metadata
real saved historical external workflow: unified Lens reopens each decision through native tools without a trainer
synthetic harness: arbitrary keys and stage names select the latest recorded decision
synthetic harness: selecting an earlier denial never substitutes the later receipt
synthetic harness: renaming every binding changes queries without editing a workflow profile
synthetic harness: absent inference evidence is omitted rather than asserted false
synthetic harness: missing bindings, unsupported schema, and non-decision stage selection reject clearly
synthetic harness: repeated cursor selection is a no-op and unavailable stops fail
The generic client accepts arbitrary profile, dataset role and shape without a digit-model contract
The public adapter routes generic worker results through v0.2 receipts, inspection and disposal
An unrequested worker profile fails initialization rather than selecting another identity protocol
A missing-identity worker response invalidates the owned session
A foreign-session worker response invalidates the owned session
A malformed worker response invalidates the owned session
A unknown-id worker response invalidates the owned session
A timed out operation terminates the worker and cannot be retried in that session
Unavailable Python reports a spawn error and repeated close remains safe
A validation receipt allows an explicit matching release policy and survives JSON persistence
Checkpoint identity follows bytes and serialization format, allowing reloads and storage relocation
Validation cannot be borrowed from different data, split semantics or preprocessing
Evaluation protocol and nested parameter changes invalidate coverage; key ordering does not
Policies apply their declared metric and direction, with inclusive threshold boundaries
Absent own metrics remain unavailable even when their names exist on Object.prototype
Freshness is explicit, with expired or future-dated evidence refused
Receipts snapshot caller-owned objects and deeply prevent later evidence mutation
Malformed, incomplete and nonfinite evidence never becomes an evaluation receipt
Malformed persisted receipts and invalid policy configuration fail closed at the release boundary
